newsitem.title: GERMANY: German leaders worry over EU rules for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: German leaders worry over EU rules for foreigners.

text.p: Leaders of Germany's powerful regional states are worried that plans to change the rights of foreigners living in the European Union could lead to an influx of immigrants into Germany, a magazine reported on Sunday.

The news weekly Focus said Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber and Kurt Beck, the leader of Rhineland-Palatinate, had asked Chancellor Helmut Kohl not to approve the part of a draft EU treaty which deals with the rights of foreigners.

The treaty, due to be concluded later this month at a summit in Amsterdam, would allow immigrants from non-EU countries the right to live and work not just in the country in which they now live but also in any state in the 15-nation bloc.

Focus said Stoiber and Beck, preparing for the summit on behalf of all the German states, feared hundreds of thousands of would come to Germany from other EU countries "to take advantage of the comparitively high German social benefits".

"If foreigners from non-EU countries can go to all the countries in the EU and have access to employment and social benefits, then Germany is threatened with massive immigration it could no longer cope with," Focus quoted Stoiber as saying.
"I'm counting on Chancellor Kohl to correct the German negotiating position on this matter," he said.
